sections.html: Magnificent pacus of the genus Mylossoma reach at most approximately 30 cm in length (the average length in nature is about half of this). They are difficult to determine to species level.

All Mylossoma species look the same in their juvenile coloration: silver with an eye spot in the middle of the body. Young animals 3-4 cm long were received from Venezuela. They are either M. albiscopum or M. aureum. Since the difference between the two species can only be seen on x-rays, and the name M. albiscopum is unknown in the aquarium world while M. aureum is mentioned here and there, the animals were called M. aureum. However, it is not excluded that it is a mixed group of both species.

The last revision from 2018 (Mateussi et al.) distinguishes 4 species south of the Andes (another species, M. acanthogaster, occurs in Lake Maracaibo, north of the Andes): M. albiscopum and M. aureum from the Amazon and Orinoco basins, M. duriventre from the Paraguay-Paraná-Uruguay basins, and M. unimaculatum from the Araguaia-Tocantins basin.
They are regarded as white water fish. M. albiscopum is one of the most important food fish in the Brazilian Amazon, while M. aureum is less important in this respect.
Keep them in a group in an accordingly large aquarium.
The water temperature should be between 24 and 30°C. They have no special requirements for water composition.
Mylossoma are mixed feeders, which in nature feed on fruits, seeds and insects. Feeding green food (chickweed, salads, dandelion etc.) can reduce plant eating.
Mylossoma are usually peaceful among each other and towards other fish. They should be kept in a group.
Planting is usually only possible with especially robust plants (Java fern, Anubias etc.), but sometimes even these are eaten.
